text: The fact this story consumes is read as follows and is written in the story as a placeholder, never as a guess: rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with an event ID, an idempotency key, a source service and a synthetic flag, and a body of caseId, decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, modelVersion, agentVersion, inputsRef, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, overrideReason, actions, outcome, decidedAt, chainSeq, prevHash, entryHash and sourceEntryRef, with the case ID as the message key. The central ledger keys its own row on (source_service, sourceEntryRef) and holds its own id in DF-DEC-001, keeps the producer chain position and hashes as received, and adds three columns of its own: source_service, source_entry_ref and ingest_at. The DecisionLogEntry that the two reads return carries the TSD P7 v2 T3.1 columns plus those three. The texts of MSG-P7-009, MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-GEN-006 stand as placeholders and are not written out.
why: No source names the fact payload, the ingest columns or the answer bodies, and a guessed payload would fix a schema on a topic that all 19 services publish to before its owner has approved it; the placeholder keeps the story buildable against a stated shape and leaves the AsyncAPI and the OpenAPI free to be published by their owners.

impact: The consumer, the three ingest columns and the two reads are built against the assumed shape; a later contract revision renames or narrows fields without a change of behaviour, because the record fields themselves are the owning service's and are only copied here

text: The five-minute collection target and the 02:00 chain-check time are held as parameter rows of rwb-case read at the version in force, assumed to be named ledger.ingest.target.minutes with value 5 and ledger.chaincheck.time with value 02:00 in the Asia/Bangkok zone; the story reads them through the parameters client of the decision-log baseline and holds no default, no fallback and no constant in Java.
why: Architecture v5 slide 28 and slide 44 JOB-14 fix the two values but no source names them as parameters, and a threshold written in code would break the rule that no value a business person may change is written in code.

text: The decision code of a reference-case step is read from the LOV-DECISION list in force and is never fixed by this story: the ledger stores the code the fact carries after validating it against the list, an unknown code is refused, and the reference-data fake supplies the route code the reference package uses, so no literal decision code appears in the story, the code, a test or a migration.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.2 omits LOV-DECISION entirely, the FSD P7 v3 field catalogue describes it as a range (D5.1 to D9.3 and X1 to X7) rather than a list, and no source fixes the code of a route move; storing the carried code behind a validation keeps the entry honest without approving a value that has no owner.

impact: One reference list and the code of one step; a later enumeration of the list adds or renames codes without a code change, because the entry stores and validates against the list in force

why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives every service its own login but no source fixes the login name of rwb-decision, and a guessed name would become a credential in a script.

text: The DP-added dependencies of section 13 — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the authorise contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON the baseline guard consumes — are built against their published contracts and their fakes and are not carried in the metadata rows; Ready to start stays Day 1, and the decision-log baseline of RWB-P7-E2024-APP is reused where it has landed.

text: The chain-check outcome is read as follows: a complete run records the count, the last chain_seq, that entry's entry_hash, the start time and the end time in the service operational report and reports no break; a break is reported the same day to Compliance and RW-AUDIT as one notification naming the case, the chain_seq and the entry_hash of the entry before it, and the check writes no decision_log_entry row of its own, because a check is not a decision of a case. The completeness gap of a late fact is reported the same way, with the case, the key and the age.
why: NFR-035 fixes the frequency and the same-day report and nothing else, and inventing a report schema or writing the check into the append-only ledger would put an operational event into a table whose every row is a decision.

text: The write-once daily seal of the ledger hash and the strict-mode acknowledgement before a point of no return are outside this story: the seal is read as a separate step of rwb-decision over this ledger with no story of RWB-E2-043, and strict mode is read as the points of no return of S4, S5, S6 and S7 reading a confirmation the ledger exposes, neither of which this story builds. The ADR-009 change Arch v5 slide 28 proposes needs Risk and Internal Audit sign-off, and that sign-off is an approval outside this run.
why: No source fixes the seal manifest, its storage path, its schedule or the confirmation operation, and building them inside the ledger story would put a write-once file step and a cross-service gate into a story whose deliverable is the append and the two reads.
